brief_extract: J. Davies, M.A., M.Sc., on the subject of Luminescence, the term coined by Wiedemann to describe the capability of an object not only to reflect light, but to radiate its own light under certain conditions apart from incandescence. Many substances and living organisms have this strange property of producing a “cold” light of different colours (as opposed to incandescent light which arises from heating) when subjected to the invisible ultra-violet rays, and although this is still a very young subject of research, its applications are already widely diverse and useful.

brief_context: Compared to luminescence for its detection qualities.
brief_extract:
By means of luminescent powders, discharge light colour effects can be improved without loss and even with increased light efficiency. title: Queen
brief_context: Accepted a carcase of frozen lamb from Australia in 1880.
brief_extract: Earlier in the same year, an epoch-making journey had been made from Sydney, Australia, to London, where, on February 2nd, the small ship the “ Strath-leven ” arrived at the East India Dock bearing the first cargo of Australian beef and mutton and a small keg of butter which had been preserved by frozen air during the 60 days’ passage across. Queen Victoria “ graciously accepted ” for her own dinner table a carcase of frozen lamb that had been killed in her Dominion of Australia, and this was a beginning of the enormous Empire export trade made possible by mechanical refrigeration. From this early phase of freezing by a stream of cold air in a charcoal-lined ship’s hold, refrigerating apparatus was gradually perfected and adapted to other needs and conditions so that a constant pre-selected low temperature could be maintained in a specially-designed cabinet or room, whatever the warmth of the outside air might be.

THE importance of the question of Nutrition was brought forward by Miss Craig McGeachy at the 1937 Conference of the British Commonwealth League in a very interesting address, from which this survey has been extracted. The problem of widespread malnutrition in every economic group in every country was first brought before an Assembly of the League of Nations in 1935.

title: Lord
brief_context: Chairman of a committee investigating nutrition and health.
brief_extract: The tragedy of the situation was heightened in that agriculturists and food producers could find no market for their products, and while there was over-production on the one hand there was underfeeding and even famine on the other. The Assembly of the League decided to set up an international enquiry into the problem, and a mixed committee of agricultural, economic and health experts, under the chairmanship of Lord Astor, was appointed to investigate the situation and to make recommendations. Their interim report, on the health aspects of nutrition, was submitted to the Assembly in 1936 and makes interesting reading for practical people, giving the food requirements for balanced diets desirable for different ages and occupations.
